questions.question_text: Respiration is the process of:
questions.explanation: Respiration releases energy from food inside living cells.

questions.question_text: Which gas do humans take in during breathing?
questions.explanation: Humans inhale oxygen from the air during breathing.

questions.question_text: Which organ helps us breathe in and out?
questions.explanation: The lungs are the main breathing organs in humans.

questions.question_text: Breathing and respiration are exactly the same thing.
questions.explanation: Breathing is the movement of air in and out of the body, while respiration is the cellular process that releases energy.

questions.question_text: Which gas is released during exhalation in larger amount than in inhaled air?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is produced during respiration and removed during exhalation.

questions.question_text: We breathe faster after running because our body needs:
questions.explanation: During exercise, the body needs more oxygen and must remove more carbon dioxide.

options.option_text: More oxygen and faster gas exchange

questions.question_text: The tiny air sacs in the lungs where exchange of gases occurs are called:
questions.explanation: Alveoli are tiny balloon-like sacs that help exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide.

questions.question_text: Respiration that uses oxygen is called:
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration happens in the presence of oxygen.

questions.question_text: All living organisms respire all the time.
questions.explanation: Respiration is necessary to release energy for life processes.

questions.question_text: Which part of the breathing system first receives the air from outside?
questions.explanation: Air usually enters the body through the nostrils.

questions.question_text: The muscle that moves downward when we inhale is the:
questions.explanation: The diaphragm contracts and moves downward during inhalation.

questions.question_text: Which statement about exhaled air is correct?
questions.explanation: Exhaled air still contains oxygen, but it has more carbon dioxide than inhaled air.

options.option_text: It contains no oxygen at all
It contains more carbon dioxide than inhaled air
It cannot support any flame because it is empty

questions.question_text: What is breathing?
questions.explanation: Breathing is the process of taking air in and pushing air out of the body.

accepted_answers: Taking air in and out of the body
Movement of air into and out of the lungs

questions.question_text: Which organism breathes through gills?
questions.explanation: Fish use gills to take dissolved oxygen from water.

questions.question_text: In cockroaches, air enters the body through small openings called:
questions.explanation: Cockroaches breathe through spiracles present on the sides of their bodies.

questions.question_text: Which structure helps earthworms exchange gases?
questions.explanation: Earthworms respire through their moist skin.

questions.question_text: Plants exchange gases mainly through tiny pores on leaves called:
questions.explanation: Stomata are small pores on leaves that allow gas exchange.

questions.question_text: Why must earthworms live in moist soil?
questions.explanation: Their skin must remain moist for respiration.

options.option_text: To keep the skin moist for breathing

questions.question_text: The number of breaths per minute is called the breathing rate.
questions.explanation: Breathing rate is measured by counting breaths taken in one minute.

questions.question_text:
Assertion: Our chest expands when we inhale.
Reason: The ribs move upward and outward during inhalation.
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.option_text: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason correctly explains Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason does not explain Assertion
Assertion is true, but Reason is false
Assertion is false, but Reason is true

questions.question_text: Why do muscles ache after very heavy exercise?
questions.explanation: When oxygen supply is insufficient, some muscle cells perform anaerobic respiration and lactic acid may accumulate.

options.option_text: Because the lungs stop working completely
Because lactic acid may form during anaerobic respiration

questions.question_text: If lime water turns milky when we breathe into it, this shows the presence of:
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide reacts with lime water and turns it milky.

questions.question_text: What happens to the diaphragm during exhalation?
questions.explanation: During exhalation, the diaphragm relaxes and moves upward, helping push air out.

questions.question_text: Which sequence is correct during inhalation?
questions.explanation: During inhalation, ribs move up and out, chest cavity expands, lungs expand, and air enters.

options.option_text: Lungs shrink -> air enters -> ribs move down
Ribs move up and out -> chest expands -> air enters
Diaphragm rises -> lungs expand -> air leaves
Air leaves -> chest expands -> ribs move inward

questions.question_text: State one difference between aerobic and anaerobic respiration.
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration uses oxygen, while anaerobic respiration occurs without oxygen.

accepted_answers: Aerobic respiration uses oxygen but anaerobic respiration does not
Aerobic needs oxygen, anaerobic happens without oxygen
Aerobic releases energy with oxygen whereas anaerobic releases energy without oxygen

questions.question_text: Why does breathing rate usually increase when climbing stairs?
questions.explanation: The body requires more energy, so more oxygen is needed and more carbon dioxide must be removed.

options.option_text: The body needs more oxygen and faster energy release

questions.question_text: Select all organisms or structures correctly matched with their breathing method.
questions.explanation: Fish use gills, earthworms use moist skin, and cockroaches use spiracles and air tubes.

questions.question_text: If a person’s chest does not expand properly during inhalation, which process is directly affected first?
questions.explanation: Air entry into the lungs depends on expansion of the chest cavity.

options.option_text: Entry of air into the lungs

questions.question_text: Why are alveoli useful in the lungs?
questions.explanation: Alveoli provide a very large surface area for exchange of gases.

options.option_text: They pump blood like the heart
They increase the surface area for gas exchange

questions.question_text: Which statement about plants and respiration is correct?
questions.explanation: Plants respire all the time, both day and night.

questions.question_text: A yeast solution is kept without much oxygen and bubbles are seen. This suggests:
questions.explanation: Yeast can respire anaerobically and release carbon dioxide bubbles.

options.option_text: The yeast has become a plant

questions.question_text: During exhalation, the ribs usually move downward and inward.
questions.explanation: That movement reduces the chest cavity volume and helps air leave the lungs.

questions.question_text: A frog lives both in water and on land. Which statement best fits its respiration?
questions.explanation: Frogs can use their skin in water and lungs on land.

options.option_text: It uses only gills throughout life
It can respire through skin in water and lungs on land

questions.question_text: Which observation best suggests that the person is inhaling rather than exhaling?
questions.explanation: During inhalation, the chest expands and air moves inward.

options.option_text: Chest becomes smaller and air moves out
Chest expands and air moves in
Diaphragm moves upward and lungs shrink
Carbon dioxide is released into lime water

questions.question_text: Why can’t an earthworm survive for long on a dry surface?
questions.explanation: Its skin must remain moist for exchange of gases. Dry skin stops proper respiration.

accepted_answers: Because its skin dries up and gas exchange becomes difficult
It breathes through moist skin, so dry conditions affect respiration
Without moisture its respiration through skin is disturbed

questions.question_text: Why does holding the breath for too long become uncomfortable mainly because of carbon dioxide buildup?
questions.explanation: The body strongly senses rising carbon dioxide levels, which triggers the urge to breathe.

options.option_text: Because rising carbon dioxide strongly stimulates the urge to breathe
Because the stomach fills with air

questions.question_text: A student compares breathing rates before and after exercise. Why must the student count for the same time interval each time?
questions.explanation: Using the same time interval makes the comparison fair and meaningful.

options.option_text: To change the number of lungs used
To reduce oxygen in the room

questions.question_text: Which setup best shows that exhaled air contains more carbon dioxide than inhaled air?
questions.explanation: Passing exhaled air through lime water turns it milky more quickly because it contains more carbon dioxide.

options.option_text: Heating oxygen in a test tube
Bubbling exhaled air through lime water
Looking at air under a microscope

questions.question_text: Which option correctly matches organism and gas-exchange structure?
questions.explanation: Fish use gills, humans use lungs, and plants mainly use stomata for gas exchange.

options.option_text: Fish - lungs; Human - spiracles; Plant - alveoli
Fish - gills; Human - lungs; Plant - stomata
Fish - skin; Human - stomata; Plant - gills
Fish - alveoli; Human - gills; Plant - spiracles

questions.question_text: Select all statements that are correct about respiration.
questions.explanation: Respiration releases energy, happens in cells, and may occur with or without oxygen in different conditions.

options.option_text: It may happen with or without oxygen depending on the organism and situation

questions.question_text: Two children run the same distance. One stops immediately and one keeps walking slowly for a minute. Why may the second child recover breathing more smoothly?
questions.explanation: Gradual slowing helps the body adjust while oxygen demand and carbon dioxide removal return toward normal.

options.option_text: Gradual slowing helps the body return toward normal breathing
Fast breathing is permanently stopped by walking

questions.question_text: Why is a large surface area important in alveoli?
questions.explanation: A larger surface area allows more efficient exchange of gases between air and blood.

options.option_text: It improves exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide

questions.question_text: Explain why breathing through the nose is usually better than breathing through the mouth.
questions.explanation: The nose helps filter, warm, and moisten incoming air before it reaches the lungs.

accepted_answers: The nose filters, warms, and moistens air
Air is cleaned and conditioned better in the nose
Nose hairs and mucus help prepare the air before it reaches the lungs

questions.question_text: Which observation would best help a student identify anaerobic respiration in muscles?
questions.explanation: Muscle fatigue or cramps after intense exercise can be linked to anaerobic respiration and lactic acid formation.

options.option_text: Expansion of a balloon in sunlight

questions.question_text: Why would blocking many stomata on a leaf affect the plant’s respiration?
questions.explanation: Stomata are important sites for gas exchange, so blocking them reduces movement of gases.

options.option_text: It would reduce gas exchange through the leaf
It would stop photosynthesis only but never affect respiration

questions.question_text: If a person inhales but the diaphragm does not contract properly, what is the most likely result?
questions.explanation: Without proper downward movement of the diaphragm, chest expansion is reduced and less air enters the lungs.

options.option_text: More oxygen is produced inside the nose

questions.question_text: To compare resting breathing rates of classmates fairly, what should be controlled first?
questions.explanation: They should all be at rest and counted over the same duration so the comparison is fair.

options.option_text: Similar resting condition and same counting time
Whether they ate the same fruit last week

questions.question_text: A cockroach’s spiracles are blocked with dust and oil. Which problem would most directly occur first?
questions.explanation: Spiracles are breathing openings, so blocking them interferes with movement of air.

options.option_text: Its wings would turn into leaves
Air entry for respiration would be disturbed
It would lose all body water instantly
Digestion would stop before breathing is affected

questions.question_text: Which evidence best supports the statement that plants also respire?
questions.explanation: Plants take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide during respiration, especially observable when photosynthesis is not occurring.

options.option_text: Plants exchange gases even when they are not photosynthesizing

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly connects breathing, blood, and cells in humans?
questions.explanation: Breathing brings oxygen into the lungs, blood carries oxygen to cells, and cells use it to release energy from food.

options.option_text: Breathing takes oxygen directly into the stomach where energy is made
Cells send oxygen to the lungs before breathing begins
Breathing brings in oxygen, blood carries it, and cells use it for respiration
Blood performs respiration outside the body
